title: Over the Covered Grain

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The reader reads the figure; the figure does not read the basket. Ask which row the pot went quiet on and the weather will answer, and the price of barley, and the row will stand where it stood. What is covered is covered; what is gone around is gone around; and the count that would join them has no hand to stand under it.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Cross, told over the second reading of Grain

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of two hundred and twenty-eight to two hundred and thirty days, six months and forty-eight days to six months and fifty days, carried everywhere and told by nobody. The surgeon's register colours the noticing --- the second Account-day's figure read over the covered grain as a number that does not know what it cost, the read figure kept beside the paid figure, the carrying arm as a record in muscle that knows weight and not cost, a plain question about a row taken apart as a surgeon takes apart a wound and set on a place of its own, the private file turned out as instruments on a towel and found exact, complete and worth nothing --- without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line; the old life stays offstage and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room or back-room interior, no hearing beyond six, no seventh of the full note, no tenth stopping before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, no fifth telling of the burned slate, no third telling of the counting room shut in the war, no fourth shaping of the pot saying, no eighth green or shape, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no opening, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read, no figure given for the dressed grain or for the hand that did not come back, no name spoken over the green or the shape, no sale or betrayal paid and no ending

scenes.title: The Day Before the Reading
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and the chapter's only drop cap: Day 228, Grain 19, Ninthday, small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf and the Clay Yard. No recap: the hand lies down against the fold after the thirtieth answer and that coordination is set down like a tool, not recalled as a sign, growth, reaching, gift or power. First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that, with the sour Ash breath of the unswept corner the house calls the thaw; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. The boy is two hundred and twenty-eight days old and six months and forty-eight days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire gives four low pulls and withholds its fifth, its payer unnamed for two hundred and twenty-eight days (T088); the river's note of water over water through the finger's-width door, the fire's gap under the floor and the boards' four nails, four and a thumb-width knot are three counts in three places that do not become one, for agreeing them would want a payer and none stands to any (T061/T082). One leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; thread frozen and unwiped; cold at cheek, temple and bare wrist-joint with the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody will perform. The file is turned out as instruments on a towel and found exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth out of a person and no seventh, three near-full answers, three shapings of the pot saying, the fourth burned-slate telling and the two shut-room tellings on their own places, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid with Grain's first reading and the true subtraction in Berr's locked box, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath unspent, three held changes on three places with the loft scrape fourth, the pale line fifth and the held inch sixth with thirty answers on it. The hand goes up an inch toward the river's note and comes down at once under conditions that have sometimes answered --- the thirty-first answer --- filed on the sixth place with no payer named, not a reach, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, key, power or rule. Morning: Sella comes to the fire before the basket, gives every instruction to the wool, fire, pot, broom, water and river wind and never to the basket, moves her lips along the two-gapped row with no figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread (T100), and sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed (T058/T079). The dressed grain lies covered near the hearth with no figure over it; the yard will go around the returning-line place with a look and no number (T098 advanced and emphatically NOT paid); cost-questions go to the pot and the weather (T077). Grain 20 stands two mornings ahead and is not brought early; the old life stays offstage with no tag and no tense-shift (T004). Last image: Sella sets the pot handle two inches beyond the hand, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting and does not look toward the bed.

scenes.title: The Kindling and the Shed
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 228, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the salt coat and hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; heat settles under the low angle, behind the pot and into the fold where one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust lies two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread is frozen and unwiped; cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the small bare wrist-joint with the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody performs. Garl is kept in objects and not a story: salt-stiff coat with the crease at the left shoulder, hollow seat with its twenty-year lean, clean dark line and the finer grey called the thaw unswept, a proverb gone to a pot with no crack, the tile debt circling without a name, his name unspoken for two hundred and twenty-eight days; no collector came up the clay road (T009/T013/T092). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed and tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count; the small knife lies at the very edge of its sill with six in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it. The sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes to his teeth, goes all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name --- a remembered stopping and not a new one --- nine stoppings stand with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, the Seed 16 breath is drawn and not spent and the loan stays uncalled; no collector came on Grain 19; chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, pale clip-ring at the left wrist, warm stone cold and unreconciled in its loft pot (T036/T076/T006). At the wheel-shed Jorra comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip; three or more men went low into the finger's-width-open back room before first grey and get no name; he speaks to the wheel before anyone (It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady), tells a pot You'll do, knows the full note three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it and keeps it back on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them; the three pot sayings stand as sayings, the burned-slate word stands at a fourth telling from Slate Row and the two shut-room tellings stay two; he grows quieter and the household straightens around the quiet without an order. When her voice goes low his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of her sentence, holds, moves a hair's breadth and is left standing --- a remembered repetition, not a change made again --- and he joins the iron to no kiln; he's not Vail stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name is neither given nor withdrawn (T035/T031/T062/T065/T095). Sella tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079/T100). At the going of the light she carries him up the clay road at the half-pace, woodsmoke before and river wind behind, goes wide around the clean dark line, the finer grey, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone ring, the bare trough, the field's empty place and the returning-line place, each with a look and a wide step and no number, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face and leaves the thread frozen. In the small hours there is no breathing number anywhere in the house; fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places; the hand is asked the second way and held to the small intake only, coming down before the letting go --- the thirty-second answer --- filed on the sixth place, not a power (T061/T082). Last image: the hand comes down before the letting-go and lies against the fold while the fire goes on in the room that warms him and the river in the room he cannot enter, neither stopping for the ear.

scenes.title: A Figure Over the Basket
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 229, Grain 20, Tenthday, the second Account-day and market of Grain, from the small hours under the Vail roof up to the Cross in the morning and the going-back at midday. New day, new date, no recap: two hundred and twenty-nine days old, six months and forty-nine days, nobody told (T071/T072); the fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and twenty-nine days (T088); first smell hot clay under tallow, first sound the kiln in fours with a gap, no market brought early into the small hours. Sella carries him up the clay road at the half-pace from every open slate, sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lies and stands half a pace off, gives the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket (T058/T079). Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner; he wipes his thumb twice on his apron before touching nothing, holds a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passes a finger over the figure, reads one in twelve, as the notice says low into the top of the crowd, the figure going twice over the basket, once for the moot and once for the households that came late, says The levy is called. It is not called by me and your house, never I, and goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness (T015/T041/T047). Hessa Rale takes the narrow slate up the road before noon edge-on to her forearm with the writing turned to her sleeve, the second strap let out for the long road and the dried pale scurf of mud unbrushed on the shortened skirt, her hand to the slate before her eyes to the crowd; to a woman at the rail she says I don't read it. I carry it. There's a difference, and the road doesn't care which, and to the woman who wants more, Cross to Greybank. Reading goes up before noon. I've got a road to walk; no figure comes off the slate, and her record-first reaching stays the eighth such hand on a place of its own (T080). The bell goes four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept beside the told (T078); the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing below the north bridge for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing, his hand to the slate before his eyes to the stalls (T090). The district's arithmetic changes for the second time in Grain and cannot be changed back: the printed figure stands unchallenged and the figure read aloud is still not the figure paid, and the true subtraction stays in Berr's locked box answering nothing for the man carried out on Day 188. The dressed grain lying covered under the Vail roof is read over by a figure that does not know what it cost, and the reading answers nothing for the hand that went in on Seed 15 and did not come back --- T098 advanced and emphatically NOT paid, no name, cause, accident, body, figure or payment. The seventh green remains a colour and the seventh shape a shape held offstage from Grain 10 with no eighth of either, no second look joined, no name, no loaf, no slate, no sale, neither woman nor child called Fenna or Ulda in the narration, neither promoted into a hearing, a cause or a romance (T050/T051 and T033/T034 held). At the market's edge the hand is asked the third way and comes down before the counted breath --- the thirty-third answer --- filed on the sixth place, not a hearing or a seventh (T061/T082). Last image: Berr's box goes up the clay road locked with the true subtraction inside while the bell's gap hangs in the square with nobody crossing himself, and the boy's hand comes down before the counted breath.

scenes.title: What the House Did Not Enter
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 229, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth, the salt coat and hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; heat settles under the low angle, behind the pot and into the fold where one stiff brown-edged barley crust lies two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread is frozen and unwiped; cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody performs. A neighbour at the door asks what the storing will take now the grain is under wool and Sella sends the question to the pot and the weather; a man come down the clay road brings a number up out of a fist toward the well, looks at it and puts it back into his sleeve so the figure arrives nowhere --- nothing priced, refused or entered (T077). With her back to the basket she moves her lips along the two-gapped row with no figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal underneath stays unread, uncounted and uncopied (T100), and does not touch the widow's mark, because an afternoon, a shelf and a basket are not openings --- no opening in forty-nine days (T058/T079). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed, says Six counted. The next I don't count, sets the knife at the very edge with six where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there as a remembered stopping with no figure and no name, keeps nine with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, draws the Seed 16 breath and does not spend it and leaves the loan uncalled; no collector came up or went down the clay road on Grain 20; the warm stone lies cold in its loft pot (T036/T076/T006). At the wheel-shed Jorra parts dust from slip as clot from vessel, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, tells a pot You'll do and withholds the note with air under it and a want, lets the three sayings stand as sayings and the burned-slate word stand at four from Slate Row, gives the men unnamed before first grey no name, and does not say the room was cold; when her voice goes low his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of her sentence, moves a hair's breadth and is left standing as a remembered repetition (T035/T031/T062/T065/T095). At the going of the light she carries him home at the half-pace and goes wide around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone round ring, the bare trough, the field's empty place and the returning-line place, each with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092/T098). The dressed grain stays covered near the hearth with its figure nowhere; Grain 21 is one morning ahead and the question that will be asked over the boards tomorrow is not brought early. In the small hours fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places; the hand is asked the fourth way and is kept to the river's own low interval with no count anywhere in the house to hold it against, coming down on the next low note --- the thirty-fourth answer --- filed on the sixth place, not a power (T061/T082/T088). Last image: the hand goes down on the river's next low note with no count in the house to hold it against and the dressed grain lies covered with no figure over it.

scenes.title: A Wrong Wind Over the Boards
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 230, Grain 21, Firstday, small hours under the Vail roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf, the Clay Yard, the drying racks, the yard well and the wheel-shed edge. New day, new date, no recap: two hundred and thirty days old, six months and fifty days, nobody told (T071/T072); the fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and thirty days (T088); first smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that, with the sour Ash breath of the corner called the thaw; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, no bell and no market. The first ordinary tending morning after the reading: the dressed grain stays under its covering near the hearth, counted in glances and handfuls and by the carrying arm's weight that knows weight and not cost, entered on no slate and given no figure; the yard goes around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone round ring, the bare trough, the field's empty place and the place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, each with a look and a wide step and no number --- T098 advanced and emphatically NOT paid, no name, cause, body, figure or payment (T077, T009/T013/T092). A wrong wind comes up off High Kiln: the sweet edge of lead glaze rides over the boards, touches the fold and goes out on the wind that brought it, a direction and not a second edge paid, the seventh green still a colour with no eighth (T064, T050/T051 held); one of the three shapings of the pot saying --- a pot gone quiet on every row come the thaw --- is let to stand again as a saying, still a saying and not a fourth likeness made a cause, with no lesson, no name for what ailed the man carried out on Day 188 and no pot lost (T061/T082). Sella sends the door's and the well's cost-questions to the pot and the weather, keeps her finger above the charcoal and leaves the widow's mark untouched --- no opening in fifty days (T058/T079/T100). Tarn keeps six where the house can check and the seventh at the lip, tells the kindling Six counted. The next I don't count, brings the ear-sentence to the calling word and stops as a remembered stopping, holds nine with no tenth and the Seed 16 breath unspent, and no collector comes on Grain 21; the warm stone lies cold in its loft pot (T036/T076/T006). Jorra comes through with meal-fine slate dust past the bent finger, parts it from slip, tells a pot You'll do, withholds the note, lets the burned-slate word stand at four and the shut-room tellings at two, puts his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence as a remembered repetition, keeps he's not Vail sealed and the promise of the boy's name ungiven (T035/T031/T062/T065/T095). The hand is asked the fifth way and comes down at once under conditions that have sometimes answered --- the thirty-fifth answer --- filed on the sixth place (T061/T082). The plain question about a row stands at the edge of the chapter's notice, held for the next scene and not brought early into the morning; Grain 30 (Day 239), the third and last Account-day and market, is nine mornings off and not brought early. Last image: a kiln-hand's voice goes over the boards with the price of barley behind it and the boy's hand comes down at once under conditions that had once answered.

scenes.title: The Row Nobody Owned
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 230, Grain 21, Firstday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. THE CHAPTER'S NEW THREAD, planted and unpaid --- T101: over the boards a plain question is asked in a voice with no owner --- which row did the pot go quiet on? --- and it is answered with the weather and the price of barley, so that the row stands where it stood, a direction arrived nowhere. The asker has no room, no hand at the kiln and no cause; the boy files the question on a place of its own with a finger between it and the three pot sayings, the fourth burned-slate telling, the two shut-room tellings, the hearings and the count. It is NOT a fourth shaping of the pot saying, NOT a hearing, NOT a seventh of the full note, NOT a cause, NOT a name and NOT a fifth telling of the slate; it is a seed for the far-off day a witness stands somewhere and can be asked. Three sayings stay three, four tellings stay four, two tellings stay two (T061/T082, T035/T031/T065/T095, T101 planted). The afternoon thins; heat settles under the low angle into the fold where one stiff brown-edged barley crust lies two inches from the ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread is frozen and unwiped; cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint with the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody performs; Garl stays kept in objects and uncalled (T009/T013/T092). Sella moves her lips along the two-gapped row with no figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, and leaves the widow's mark untouched --- no opening in fifty days, because an afternoon, a shelf, a basket and a bed are not openings (T058/T079/T100). At the kindling Tarn keeps six and the seventh at the lip, stops the ear-sentence short of the calling word as a remembered stopping, holds nine with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, keeps the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled, and no collector comes on Grain 21; the warm stone lies cold in its loft pot (T036/T076/T006). At the shed Jorra lets the one saying stand as a saying on the wrong wind, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, withholds the note, stands the burned-slate word at four and the shut-room tellings at two, and puts his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's sentence as a remembered repetition; he's not Vail stays sealed and the promise stays ungiven. At the going of the light she carries him up at the half-pace, woodsmoke before and river wind behind, goes wide around the clean dark line, the finer grey, the rack space, the pan's ring, the bare trough, the field's empty place and the returning-line place with a look and a wide step and no number, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face and leaves the thread frozen. She goes to her own bed before the small hours and leaves the coals to keep themselves, and there is no breathing number anywhere in the house; the two rooms do not touch; fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places and none rises into another, for agreeing them would want a payer and none stands to any (T088, T061/T082). The file is exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers, three pot sayings, the fourth burned-slate telling, the two shut-room tellings, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid, nine stoppings with no tenth, three held changes on three places with the loft scrape fourth, the pale line fifth and the held inch sixth, the seed of T101 on a new place of its own. The hand is asked the sixth way and goes up an inch toward the river's note, is carried through the small intake, the hold and the letting go of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire in the room that does not touch his, kept through the little silence after her count has ended and brought down on the river's next low note --- the thirty-sixth answer, a two-rhythm coordination held across the wall, remembered, not a change made again, filed on the sixth place with no payer named, NOT a longer reach, a miss entered, a hearing, a seventh, a tenth stopping, a payment, a held change, a key, a power or a rule. Two hundred and thirty stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody in Sarn, Sill or Grath; the fire's fifth is unpaid for two hundred and thirty days; the seventh year stands at its very end and has not given; the seventh green is a colour and the seventh shape a shape gathered and unjoined; the dressed grain lies covered near the hearth with the place in the returning line still gone around and still without a number; the question about the row stands over the boards with nobody to own it. Grain 30 (Day 239), the third and last Account-day and market, stands nine mornings ahead and is not brought early. Forward into Day 231, Grain 22, Secondday, Chapter 60. Last image: the hand comes down on the river's next low note and the count goes forward exact and unspent into Day 231 while a question about a row stands over the boards with nobody to own it and the dressed grain lies covered with no figure over it.
